summary: A card for a neck collar cut from one sheet that snaps open with a twist and locks without glue.
license_note: MIT covers this card, and the grant clause is in examples/kaze-card/LICENSE. NOTICE at https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/NOTICE.txt lists what the project cannot grant; nothing here enlarges or narrows it.
origin: Not a fork and not a repository of its own. This is a page-project inside mrdirno/vibe-cards, published on that repo's Pages surface, and its host repo's MIT is inherited by the code around the card rather than chosen for the design. The package arrived from another system. The consumed-capability list it ships names a tab-and-slot solver from MANIS-CUIRASS-001 that does not exist in that package: the list is an intent the package recorded, not an inventory a reader can call.
_note: L0, not L1. L0's clauses hold: this manifest is served at the url the card's chip carries, the page it names carries an account-free wishing well, and the repository has a LICENSE with a real SPDX id. L1 is not claimed on either of its added clauses. docs/EVALS.md is Card Studio's eval record, not this card's, so shipped changes here do not carry an eval meeting section 2. And nobody has built this object, so every dimension on the card is drawing arithmetic rather than a fit someone has measured. Section 3 says L0 when in doubt. examples/kaze-card/docs/AUTHORSHIP.md discloses human intent, selections and arrangements, and identifies the AI-generated portions. A chip for this card was written and read back on hardware 2026-08-16. This file states stable facts about this card only. An earlier version embedded byte counts, grep tallies and claims about what other files currently say; every one of those was falsified by the same commit that published them, including one that had claimed this very url was unreachable — a claim that would have been served inside the successful response to fetching it. A manifest that measures its own repository is false on arrival, so this one states no measurement at all.
